original_value: AbstractAccurate precipitation estimation is significant since it matters to everyone on social and economic activities and is of great importance to monitor and forecast disasters. The traditional method utilizes an exponential relation between radar reflectivity factors and precipitation called Z-R relationship which has a low accuracy in precipitation estimation. With the rapid development of computing power in cloud computing, recent researches show that artificial intelligence is a promising approach, especially deep learning approaches in learning accurate patterns and appear well suited for the task of precipitation estimation, given an ample account of radar data. In this study, we introduce these approaches to the precipitation estimation, proposing two models based on the back propagation neural networks (BPNN) and convolutional neural networks (CNN) respectively, to compare with the traditional method in meteorological service systems. The results of the three approaches show that deep learning algorithms outperform the traditional method with 75.84% and 82.30% lower mean square errors respectively. Meanwhile, the proposed method with CNN achieves a better performance than that with BPNN for its ability to preserve the spatial information by maintaining the interconnection between pixels, which improves 26.75% compared to that with BPNN.

result.paraphrase: Accurate precipitation estimation is important because it affects social and economic activities and is crucial for disaster monitoring and forecasting. The conventional approach uses an exponential Z-R relationship between radar reflectivity and precipitation, but it has low estimation accuracy. With the rapid growth of cloud-computing power, recent studies suggest that artificial intelligence is promising, especially deep learning methods that can learn accurate patterns and are well suited to precipitation estimation when ample radar data are available. In this study, we apply these approaches to precipitation estimation and propose two models based respectively on back propagation neural networks (BPNN) and convolutional neural networks (CNN) for comparison with the traditional method in meteorological service systems. The results show that the three approaches indicate deep learning algorithms outperform the traditional method, with mean square errors reduced by 75.84% and 82.30% respectively. In addition, the CNN-based proposed method performs better than the BPNN-based one because it preserves spatial information by maintaining pixel interconnections, improving by 26.75% over BPNN.
